voice_note: Warm, dry, unhurried. A storyteller who has run a hundred sessions. Never salesy.

segments.text: It's twenty to seven. Your game starts at half past. And you have nothing prepared.
segments.beat: Hero: dark table, lamplight, module lying on the wood.

segments.text: OneShotsmith forges a complete Dungeons and Dragons one-shot in your browser. A keyed map. Encounters costed against the real rulebook math. A villain with an actual plan. No account, no server, and no AI anywhere in the generator.
segments.beat: Scroll the module: map, title, scenes.

segments.text: It also registers eight WebMCP tools. So the AI in my browser doesn't have to squint at the page and guess. It can just call it.
One sentence. The agent picks the theme, sets the table, and the module appears. Map, scenes, encounters, treasure. Every number correct.
Now the part no screen-scraper could ever do. Keep the map. Give me a different villain. One section re-rolls. Everything else stays byte for byte identical, because every section rolls its own dice.
segments.beat: THE MONEY SHOT. reroll_section; villain changes, map does not.

segments.text: Someone drops out. Someone brings a level eight. Every fight is re-costed against the actual Dungeon Master's Guide thresholds, and the story never moves an inch.
segments.beat: adjust_party; XP numbers change, title and villain hold.

segments.text: Ask it about scene three, and it reads the real scene. The page hands over the text. The model gives it a voice. Neither one is guessing.
segments.beat: get_scene returns; scroll the scene with read-aloud box.

segments.text: Then print it like it's nineteen eighty-one. Boxed text, keyed entries, and a player map on its own page.
And the link regenerates it exactly. Same map, same villain, same maths. Forever.
segments.beat: Paste permalink in a clean window; identical module.

segments.text: The agent brings the language. The page brings the map, the maths, and the memory. Neither can do it alone. That's the whole idea.
segments.beat: Pull back to the lamplit table. End card.
